set.body:
Scope

Build on ResponseBasis, BasisCoefficients, and BasisTransform. Do not replace the causal HRF/pulse core.

Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every built-in basis element has a stable BasisElementId and semantic BasisRole, including canonical, temporal derivative, dispersion derivative, FIR bin/window, spline/Fourier component where meaningful, and custom.
- [ ] Custom bases must supply stable element identities/labels and validated cardinality; a claimed width cannot silently disagree with evaluated values.
- [ ] Coefficient selection by role is distinct from a joint basis omnibus.
- [ ] Linear response functionals support at-time, prespecified window mean, and window integral semantics and compile to basis weights with documented discretization.
- [ ] No API defaults to averaging arbitrary basis coefficients.
- [ ] Requesting a role absent from a basis returns a typed error, or fails statically where the basis type genuinely makes that fact available.
- [ ] Response reconstruction carries units/scaling conventions and remains compatible with current shared/per-column normalization receipts.
- [ ] Supported basis permutation and transform laws preserve reconstructed responses, fitted values, covariance transport, and adjusted hypotheses within condition-aware tolerances.
- [ ] Nonlinear summaries such as peak latency are represented separately and cannot masquerade as linear contrasts.
- [ ] HRF, law, design, and contrast tests pass on JVM and Scala.js.
set.title: P1.4: add stable basis roles and explicit response-level linear functionals
